routes.label: Find a repeating pair by exact arithmetic

question: The first two terms of a sequence are \(a_1 = 1\) and \(a_2 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}.\) For \(n \ge 1,\) \[a_{n+2} = \dfrac{a_n + a_{n+1}}{1 - a_n a_{n+1}}.\] What is \(|a_{2009}|?\)
solution:
The recurrence uses two preceding terms, so repeating one value is not enough to establish a cycle. We look for a repeated consecutive pair, because that pair determines every subsequent term.

To keep the arithmetic short, write
\[
r=\sqrt3,\qquad p=2+r,\qquad q=2-r.
\]
Then \(r^2=3\), \(pq=1\), and \(p>r>1\). The first new terms are
\[
a_3=\frac{1+1/r}{1-1/r}=\frac{r+1}{r-1}=p,
\]
\[
a_4=\frac{1/r+p}{1-p/r}=-p,
\qquad
 a_5=\frac{p-p}{1+p^2}=0.
\]
Continuing the same substitutions, simplifying with \(r^2=3\) and \(pq=1\), gives
\[
(a_1,\ldots,a_6)=(1,1/r,p,-p,0,-p),
\]
\[
(a_7,\ldots,a_{12})=(-p,1/r,-1,-q,-r,-p),
\]
\[
(a_{13},\ldots,a_{18})=(1,-1/r,q,-q,0,-q),
\]
\[
(a_{19},\ldots,a_{24})=(-q,-1/r,-1,-p,r,-q),
\]
and finally
\[
(a_{25},a_{26})=(1,1/r)=(a_1,a_2).
\]
For example, the transition from the two consecutive values \(-p,-p\) is simplified by
\[
\frac{-2p}{1-p^2}=\frac{2p}{p^2-1}=\frac1r,
\]
since \(p^2-1=2rp\).

We must check that none of these steps divides by zero. Among the consecutive products in the displayed cycle, every positive product belongs to one of these two lists:
\[
1/r,\ q,\ qr,\ q^2,\ q/r<1,
\]
\[
p,\ p/r,\ pr,\ p^2>1.
\]
These comparisons follow from \(p>r>1\) and \(q=1/p\); in particular, \(qr=r/p<1\). Every other consecutive product is nonpositive. Thus no consecutive product equals \(1\), so every recurrence denominator is nonzero.

The initial pair has returned after 24 steps. Since every pair determines the next pair and all denominators in the cycle are valid, the same block repeats indefinitely:
\[
a_{n+24}=a_n\qquad(n\ge1).
\]
Now \(2009=24\cdot83+17\), and the displayed values give \(a_{17}=0\). Therefore \(|a_{2009}|=\boxed{0}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
